definition_en: to push someone or something roughly or forcefully
core_image: 一只手掌狠狠顶上去，把人逼得踉跄
scene: 人群里有人猛推了他一把。Someone shoved him hard in the crowded hallway.
sceneCN: 这里 shove 是「猛推」（第 1 个义项：用力推开人或物）；句意：在拥挤的走廊里有人狠狠推了他一把。

derivatives.zh: 现在分词名词化，义为「推挤（行为）」
与 shove 同源的名词，义为「铲子；铲」

senses.title: To push roughly
senses.definition: to push someone or something roughly or forcefully
senses.definitionCN: 粗暴或用力地推开某人或某物
senses.example: The guard shoved the crowd back.
senses.why: The core image is a hand driving force into someone, rougher than a gentle push.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是用手把力道砸进对方身上，比普通的推更粗暴，所以引出「猛推」义。

senses.title: To push something carelessly into a place
senses.definition: to put something somewhere quickly and carelessly
senses.definitionCN: 把某物随手快速塞到某个地方
senses.example: He shoved the papers into his bag.
senses.exampleCN: 他把文件胡乱塞进包里。
senses.why: Forcing things into a space is the same rough pushing motion applied to objects.
senses.whyCN: 把东西硬塞进空间，就是把「用力推」的动作用到物品上，义项由此延伸。

senses.title: To move oneself through a crowd
senses.definition: to push your way through a place or past people
senses.example: She shoved past the reporters.
senses.exampleCN: 她从记者中间挤了过去。
senses.why: When the pusher and the mover are the same person, rough pushing becomes shoving through.
senses.whyCN: 当施力者与移动者是同一人，「猛推」就变成替自己开路的「挤」，义项随之成立。

senses.title: A rough push
senses.definition: a strong, rough push
senses.example: He gave the door a hard shove.
senses.exampleCN: 他猛地推了一下那扇门。
senses.why: The action names the event itself, turning the motion into a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 动作本身被当作事件命名，推的行为变成了可数的名词，义项由动词转来。

intro.en: Shove is an old native English word for pushing with force.
intro.cn: shove 是英语本土的古老动词，本义就是用力推。

items.en: A reconstructed root *skeub- meant to push or shove.
items.cn: 重构词根 *skeub- 意为推、撞。

items.en: Scufan meant to push away or thrust.
items.cn: 古英语 scufan 意为推开、猛推。

items.en: The form evolved into shoven, keeping the pushing sense.
items.cn: 中古英语演变为 shoven，仍保留推的意义。

items.en: The careless sense of stuffing things into places appeared.
items.cn: 「胡乱塞进」的用法在这个时期出现。

items.en: The noun sense and the crowded-passage sense are both common today.
items.cn: 名词用法与「挤过去」的用法今天都很常用。

note.en: Shove is compared with its close relative shove- words and with other pushing verbs.
note.cn: 把 shove 与同族词以及其它表示推的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a tool with a broad blade for moving earth, or to move it with such a tool
entries.definitionCN: 铲子；用铲子铲，与 shove 同源于「推、掷」的动作

entries.definition: to walk by dragging the feet, or to mix cards
entries.definitionCN: 拖着脚走；洗牌，只是拼拼写近，词源与 shove 无关
关闭，拼写相近但来源不同

entries.definition: to press something to move it away from you
entries.definitionCN: 推，中性常用词，语气不如 shove 粗暴
猛地一推、捅，强调突然发力

entries.definition: to push roughly against someone in a crowd
entries.definitionCN: 在人群中推挤、碰撞，强调拥挤场面

normalIntro.en: Shove pictures a hand driving into someone with force.
normalIntro.cn: shove 的画面是一只手带着力道顶上去。

normal.en: Someone shoved him hard in the hallway.
normal.cn: 走廊里有人狠狠推了他一把。

normal.en: He shoved the papers into his bag.
normal.cn: 他把文件胡乱塞进包里。

normal.en: She shoved past the reporters.
normal.cn: 她从记者中间挤了过去。

normal.en: He gave the door a hard shove.
normal.cn: 他猛地推了一下那扇门。

normal.en: Stop shoving in the queue.

abstract.en: A shove is a push without politeness.
abstract.cn: shove 是不带礼貌的推。

abstract.en: Life sometimes shoves you off balance.
abstract.cn: 生活有时会把你猛推得站不稳。

abstract.en: One shove can start an argument.
abstract.cn: 一记猛推就能挑起争吵。

examples.en: Someone shoved him hard in the crowded hallway.
examples.cn: 在拥挤的走廊里有人狠狠推了他一把。

examples.en: He shoved the papers into his bag and left.
examples.cn: 他把文件胡乱塞进包里就走了。

examples.en: The guard shoved the crowd back from the gate.
examples.cn: 警卫把人群从大门口往后推。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沙夫」——想象一只手掌拍在背上「沙」的一声，人就「伏」了下去，这就是被人猛推一把的 shove。

root: 源自古英语 scufan（推开、猛推），一般可追溯到日耳曼语词根 *skeub-（推、撞），与 shovel（铲子）同源。

sensesIntro.en: Shove means to push roughly, to stuff things carelessly, to push through, or the push itself as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: shove 既指粗暴地推，也指胡乱塞放、挤过去，还可作名词指猛推的动作。

core.en: A hand driving force into someone or something.
core.cn: 一只手把力道砸进人或物身上。

branches.en: The guard drives the crowd back with rough force.
branches.cn: 警卫用粗暴的力道把人群顶回去。

branches.en: The pushing motion becomes stuffing things carelessly.
branches.cn: 推的动作变成胡乱塞放东西。

branches.en: The pusher pushes himself through the crowd.
branches.cn: 施力者用推给自己在人群里开路。

branches.en: The action names the rough push itself.
branches.cn: 动作反过来命名那次猛推。

branches.en: All senses share one rough, careless force.
branches.cn: 各义项共享同一股粗暴随意的力。

intro.en: Shove is a short native verb whose family comes from an old pushing root.
intro.cn: shove 是简短的本土动词，其词族源自古老的「推」词根。

latinIntro.en: Shove is Germanic, not Latin, so no Latin relatives exist; the Germanic family is listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: shove 属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，没有拉丁同族词，此处列出日耳曼语词族。

items.exampleCN: 有人从背后猛推了他一下。

items.structure: Old English scofl, from the same pushing root
items.meaning: a tool for pushing and lifting earth
items.example: He shoveled snow off the path.
There was a lot of shoving at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 大门口发生了不少推挤。

items.meaning: to leave; to push a boat away from shore
items.example: It is late; we should shove off.

items.meaning: to treat someone roughly or bossily
items.example: I will not be shoved around.

items.meaning: to press something to move it away
items.example: Push the door, do not pull.
He thrust the letter into his pocket.

items.meaning: to drag the feet or mix cards

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「推挤行为」

definition_en: to let someone see something, to prove or make clear, or a performance or display
core_image: 幕布拉开，舞台灯光把一切摊在观众眼前
scene: 她把照片给大家看。She showed the photo to everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 show 是「展示」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把照片给大家看。

senses.title: To display
senses.definition: to let someone see something
senses.example: She showed the photo to everyone.
senses.why: This is the basic visual sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的视觉义项。

senses.title: To make clear
senses.definition: to prove or make something clear
senses.example: The test showed that he was right.
senses.why: Showing something makes it visible to reason.
senses.whyCN: 展示某物就是让它对理性可见。

senses.title: A performance
senses.definition: a play, concert, or other public performance
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧、音乐会或其他公开演出
senses.example: We saw a show at the theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在剧院看了一场演出。
senses.why: The noun grew from something put before an audience.
senses.whyCN: 名词义源于呈现在观众面前的东西。

senses.title: An exhibition
senses.definition: a public display of objects or art
senses.definitionCN: 物品或艺术的公开展示
senses.example: The flower show opens on Friday.
senses.why: Objects, like performances, are shown to the public.
senses.whyCN: 物品和演出一样，都是向公众展示的。

intro.en: Show comes from an old word meaning to look at.
intro.cn: show 来自一个意为「看」的古老词。

items.en: Sceawian meant to look at or inspect.
Shewen came to mean to display.
The verb added the sense to prove.
items.cn: 动词增添了证明的义项。

items.en: The noun named a public performance.
Exhibitions and broadcasts widened the noun.
items.cn: 展览与广播扩大了名词的用法。

note.en: Show is compared with similar-looking words and with words for displaying.
note.cn: 把 show 与形近词以及表示展示的词作比较。

entries.definition: a fall of rain or a wash
to put something where it can be seen

normalIntro.en: To show is to move something from hidden to seen.
normalIntro.cn: show 就是把东西从看不见的地方移到看得见的地方。

normal.en: She showed the photo to everyone.
The test showed that he was right.
We saw a show at the theatre.
normal.cn: 我们在剧院看了一场演出。

normal.en: The flower show opens on Friday.
He showed me around the city.
normal.cn: 他带我参观了这座城市。

abstract.en: A show is a secret given light.
abstract.cn: 演出是重见光明的秘密。

abstract.en: To show is to lend your eyes to another.
abstract.cn: 展示就是把你的眼睛借给别人。

abstract.en: Proof is a fact put on stage.
abstract.cn: 证据是被搬上舞台的事实。

examples.en: She showed the photo to everyone.
The test showed that he was right.
We saw a show at the theatre.
examples.cn: 我们在剧院看了一场演出。

dict_mnemonic.text: show 的核心是「让人看见」：给人看照片是展示，让证据被看见是表明，把节目摆上台是演出。

root: 源自古英语 sceawian（看、察看），核心义「使某物进入视线」。

sensesIntro.en: Show means to display, to make clear, a performance, or an exhibition.
sensesIntro.cn: show 意为展示、表明、演出或展览。

core.en: Moving something from hidden into sight.
core.cn: 把某物从隐蔽处移到视线中。

branches.en: The object is offered to the eyes.
The fact is made visible to reason.
People gather to watch.
Objects stand still for viewing.
Display and performance share one act of showing.
branches.cn: 展示与演出共享同一个呈现动作。

intro.en: Show builds a family of display and performance words.
intro.cn: show 构成表示展示与表演的词族。

latinIntro.en: Show is Germanic; Latin monstrare, to show, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: show 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 monstrare（展示）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The film was shown last night.

items.meaning: a glass case for displaying goods
items.example: The rings are in the showcase.
He is a bit of a show-off.

items.exampleCN: 演艺经理介绍了这个节目。

definition_zh: 淋浴；阵雨；送礼聚会；大量给予
definition_en: a wash under falling water, a short fall of rain, a party for giving gifts, or to give many things
core_image: 花洒喷出细密水线，热气在浴室里升起
scene: 他每天早上冲个淋浴。He takes a shower every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 shower 是「淋浴」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他每天早上冲个淋浴。

senses.title: A wash
senses.definition: a wash under a spray of falling water
senses.example: He takes a shower every morning.
senses.why: This is the everyday bathroom sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常浴室场景中的义项。

senses.title: A rain
senses.definition: a short fall of rain
senses.example: A shower passed over the town.
senses.why: Falling water connects rain and washing.
senses.whyCN: 落下的水流把雨和淋浴联系起来。

senses.title: A gift party
senses.definition: a party where gifts are given, especially for a baby or a bride
senses.definitionCN: 赠送礼物的聚会，尤指为婴儿或新娘举办
senses.example: They held a baby shower for her.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为她办了一场迎婴聚会。
senses.why: Gifts fall on the guest like rain.
senses.whyCN: 礼物像雨一样落在客人身上。

senses.title: To give much
senses.definition: to give someone many things or much attention
senses.definitionCN: 给某人许多东西或大量关注
senses.example: Fans showered her with flowers.
senses.why: The rain image turns into an abundance of gifts.
senses.whyCN: 雨的意象转化为礼物的丰盛。

intro.en: Shower first meant a brief fall of rain.
intro.cn: shower 最初意为一阵短暂的降雨。

items.en: Scur meant a brief storm or shower.
items.cn: scur 意为短暂的暴风雨或阵雨。

items.en: Shour named a fall of rain.
The washing sense appeared with indoor plumbing.
items.cn: 随着室内管道出现，淋浴义项产生了。

items.en: A party for giving gifts took the name.
items.cn: 赠送礼物的聚会沿用了这个词。

items.en: The verb came to mean to give in large amounts.
items.cn: 动词义发展为大量给予。

note.en: Shower is compared with similar-looking words and with words for washing and rain.
note.cn: 把 shower 与形近词以及表示洗浴和降雨的词作比较。

entries.definition: a wash in a tub of water

normalIntro.en: A shower is rain invited indoors, or gifts falling like rain.
normalIntro.cn: shower 是被请进室内的雨，或像雨一样落下的礼物。

normal.en: He takes a shower every morning.
A shower passed over the town.
They held a baby shower for her.
normal.cn: 他们为她办了一场迎婴聚会。

normal.en: Fans showered her with flowers.
The showerhead is broken.

abstract.en: A shower is rain that agrees to stay in one room.
abstract.cn: 淋浴是愿意留在一个房间里的雨。

abstract.en: Gifts can fall as softly as warm rain.
abstract.cn: 礼物可以像暖雨一样轻轻落下。

abstract.en: Kindness often arrives in showers, not drops.
abstract.cn: 善意常常成阵而来，而非一滴一滴。

examples.en: He takes a shower every morning.
A shower passed over the town.
Fans showered her with flowers.

dict_mnemonic.text: shower 本来是「一阵雨」：水从上往下落，落在身上是淋浴，落在礼物上就是大量赠送。

root: 源自古英语 scur（短暂风雨、阵雨），核心义「从上方落下的一阵水或物」。

sensesIntro.en: Shower means a wash, a short rain, a gift party, or to give in large amounts.
sensesIntro.cn: shower 意为淋浴、阵雨、送礼聚会或大量给予。

core.en: Water or gifts falling from above in a short burst.
core.cn: 水或礼物从上方短促地落下。

branches.en: Water falls on a standing body.
Clouds release a brief rain.
Friends gather to give gifts.
branches.cn: 朋友们聚在一起送礼物。

branches.en: Gifts and praise pour down.
Rain and generosity share the same falling shape.
branches.cn: 雨与慷慨共享同一种下落形态。

intro.en: Shower builds a small family of rain and bathroom words.
intro.cn: shower 构成表示降雨与浴室用品的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shower is Germanic; Latin imber, a rain shower, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shower 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 imber（阵雨）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: a brief rain or a wash

items.exampleCN: 他很快洗了澡穿好衣服。

items.example: The shower gel smells of lemon.

items.meaning: a cap that keeps hair dry

definition_zh: 耸肩；表示怀疑；不理会；耸肩动作
definition_en: to raise the shoulders to show doubt or indifference, to dismiss something, or such a movement
core_image: 一个人双肩一抬，嘴角一撇，表示自己也不知道
scene: 他耸耸肩说不知道。He shrugged and said he did not know.
sceneCN: 这里 shrug 是「耸肩」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他耸耸肩说不知道。

senses.title: To raise the shoulders
senses.definition: to raise the shoulders slightly
senses.example: He shrugged and said he did not know.
senses.why: This is the basic gesture.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的手势义项。

senses.title: To show doubt
senses.definition: to use the gesture to show doubt
senses.example: She shrugged at my question.
senses.exampleCN: 她对我的问题耸了耸肩。
senses.why: The movement answers a question without words.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作不用语言就回答了问题。

senses.title: To dismiss
senses.definition: to treat something as unimportant
senses.example: He shrugged off the criticism.
senses.why: The gesture can push a problem away.
senses.whyCN: 这个手势可以把问题推开。

senses.title: The movement
senses.definition: the act of raising the shoulders
senses.example: She answered with a shrug.
senses.why: The verb turns into a noun for the gesture.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为表示该手势的名词。

intro.en: Shrug is a Middle English word whose deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: shrug 是中东英语词，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Shruggen meant to raise the shoulders.
The word may echo the movement itself.
items.cn: 这个词可能模仿动作本身。

items.en: The gesture became a sign of doubt.
items.cn: 这个手势成为怀疑的标志。

items.en: Shrug off came to mean to dismiss.
items.cn: shrug off 逐渐表示不理会。

items.en: The noun named the movement itself.

note.en: Shrug is compared with similar-looking words and with words for gestures and dismissal.
note.cn: 把 shrug 与形近词以及表示手势和不予理会的词作比较。

entries.definition: to move the head up and down
to decide something is not important

normalIntro.en: A shrug is a sentence spoken with the shoulders.
normalIntro.cn: 耸肩是用肩膀说出的一句话。

normal.en: He shrugged and said he did not know.
She shrugged at my question.
normal.cn: 她对我的问题耸了耸肩。

normal.en: He shrugged off the criticism.
She answered with a shrug.
Do not shrug away your chance.

abstract.en: A shrug says what words are too tired to say.
abstract.cn: 耸肩说出了词语累得说不出口的话。

abstract.en: To shrug off a burden is to set it down.
abstract.cn: 甩开负担就是把它放下。

abstract.en: The smallest gesture can close a long argument.
abstract.cn: 最小的手势也能结束一场长争论。

examples.en: He shrugged and said he did not know.
She answered with a shrug.
He shrugged off the criticism.

dict_mnemonic.text: shrug 把两个肩膀往上一抬：抬起来表示不知道，抬完放下表示不在乎。

root: 源自中古英语 shruggen（抬肩），核心义「用肩部动作表达态度」。

sensesIntro.en: Shrug means to raise the shoulders, show doubt, dismiss something, or such a movement.
sensesIntro.cn: shrug 意为耸肩、表示怀疑、不理会或耸肩动作。

core.en: Shoulders rise to say what words will not.
core.cn: 双肩抬起，说出词语不愿说的话。

branches.en: The shoulders move upward.
The body admits it does not know.
The gesture pushes a problem away.
The movement becomes a noun.
Doubt and dismissal share the same small motion.
branches.cn: 怀疑与不理会共享同一个小动作。

intro.en: Shrug builds a small family of gesture words.
intro.cn: shrug 构成表示手势的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shrug is Germanic; Latin gestus, a gesture, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shrug 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 gestus（手势）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She shrugs when she is unsure.
She stood shrugging at the door.

items.meaning: to push away with a shrug

definition_en: to close something, to stop operating, to block, or to keep someone or something inside
core_image: 一扇门被轻轻带上，锁舌咔哒一声扣住
scene: 请把门关上。Please shut the door.
sceneCN: 这里 shut 是「关上」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把门关上。

senses.title: To close
senses.definition: to close a door, window, or container
senses.example: Please shut the door.
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To stop operating
senses.definition: to close a business or machine
senses.example: The factory shut last month.
senses.why: A closed place stops working like a closed door.
senses.whyCN: 关闭的场所像关上的门一样停止运作。

senses.title: To block
senses.definition: to block an opening or a view
senses.example: The curtain shuts out the light.
senses.why: Closing can mean keeping something out.
senses.whyCN: 关闭也可以表示把某物挡在外面。

senses.title: To confine
senses.definition: to keep someone or something inside
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物关在里面
senses.example: They shut the dog in the yard.
senses.why: Closing can also keep something in.
senses.whyCN: 关闭也可以表示把某物关在里面。

intro.en: Shut comes from an Old English verb for bolting a door.
intro.cn: shut 来自古英语中表示给门上门闩的动词。

items.en: Scyttan meant to bolt or bar a door.
items.cn: scyttan 意为给门上门闩或横闩。

items.en: Shutten widened to mean to close.
The word covered windows and containers.
items.cn: 这个词覆盖了窗户和容器。

items.en: Businesses could shut for the day.
Shut in and shut out split the idea of closure.
items.cn: shut in 与 shut out 分化了关闭的方向。

note.en: Shut is compared with similar-looking words and with words for closing.
note.cn: 把 shut 与形近词以及表示关闭的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To shut is to make an opening stop being open.
normalIntro.cn: shut 就是让一个开口不再敞开。

normal.en: Please shut the door.
The factory shut last month.
The curtain shuts out the light.
They shut the dog in the yard.
Shut the window before you leave.

abstract.en: A shut door is a promise of privacy.
abstract.cn: 关上的门是隐私的承诺。

abstract.en: Shutting out noise can be a kindness.
abstract.cn: 把噪声挡在外面也可以是一种善意。

abstract.en: Some doors must shut before others open.
abstract.cn: 有些门必须先关上，别的门才会打开。

examples.en: Please shut the door.
The factory shut last month.
The curtain shuts out the light.

dict_mnemonic.text: shut 的核心是「合上」：门合上是关门，厂子合上是停业，帘子合上就把光挡在外面。

root: 源自古英语 scyttan（上门闩），核心义「合拢、封闭开口」。

sensesIntro.en: Shut means to close, to stop operating, to block, or to confine.
sensesIntro.cn: shut 意为关上、停业、挡住或关住。

core.en: Closing an opening so that passage stops.

branches.en: The door meets its frame.
The business stops its work.
Light and sound stay outside.
What is inside stays inside.
Closing works in both directions.
branches.cn: 关闭在两个方向上都起作用。

intro.en: Shut builds a family of closure words.
intro.cn: shut 构成表示封闭的词族。

latinIntro.en: Shut is Germanic; Latin claudere, to close, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shut 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 claudere（关闭）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: a closing of a business or machine
a person who rarely goes out
items.exampleCN: 这位闭门不出的人需要陪伴。

items.meaning: a game where one side scores nothing
items.example: The team won by a shutout.
items.exampleCN: 这支球队零封对手获胜。

definition_en: ill, feeling nausea, or tired of something
core_image: 一个人裹着毯子躺在床上，脸色发白
scene: 他今天没来上学，因为他病了。He is sick and did not come to school today.
sceneCN: 这里 sick 是「生病的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他今天病了，没有来上学。

senses.title: Ill
senses.definition: not healthy; suffering from an illness
senses.example: He is sick and stays in bed.
senses.why: This is the basic health sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的健康义项。

senses.title: Feeling nausea
senses.definition: feeling that you want to vomit
senses.example: The smell made me sick.
senses.why: The stomach sense grew out of illness.
senses.whyCN: 胃部不适的义项由生病延伸而来。

senses.title: Tired of something
senses.definition: bored or annoyed with something
senses.example: I am sick of waiting.
senses.why: Repeated annoyance feels like a kind of illness.
senses.whyCN: 反复的厌烦像一种心理上的病。

intro.en: Sick is an old English word for illness.
intro.cn: sick 是一个表示疾病的古老英语词。

items.en: Seoc meant ill or diseased.
items.cn: seoc 意为生病的、有病的。

items.en: The form became sik.
The spelling settled as sick.
The sense widened to nausea.
Informal slang gave it the sense of excellent.
items.cn: 口语俚语又赋予它「极好」的意思。

note.en: Sick is compared with similar-looking words and with other words for illness.
note.cn: 把 sick 与形近词以及其他表示疾病的词作比较。

entries.definition: a soft covering for the foot

normalIntro.en: Sick points at the body, the stomach, and the patience.
normalIntro.cn: sick 可以指向身体、胃和耐心三个方面。

normal.en: He is sick and stays in bed.
The smell made me sick.
I am sick of waiting.
She felt sick on the boat.
Sick children stayed home.

abstract.en: A sick body teaches the mind patience.
abstract.cn: 生病的身体教会心灵耐心。

abstract.en: Nausea is the stomach writing a warning.
abstract.cn: 恶心是胃写下的警告。

abstract.en: Being sick of something is a kind of tiredness.
abstract.cn: 对某事厌倦也是一种疲惫。

examples.en: He is sick and stays in bed.
The smell made me sick.
I am sick of waiting.

dict_mnemonic.text: sick 记住三个方向：身体生病、胃里恶心、心里厌烦；一个词管三处不适。

root: 源自古英语 sēoc（有病的），核心义「身体不适」。

sensesIntro.en: Sick means ill, feeling nausea, or tired of something.
sensesIntro.cn: sick 意为生病的、恶心的或厌倦的。

core.en: The body out of balance.

branches.en: Illness keeps him in bed.
A smell turns the stomach.
Waiting wears patience thin.
Both senses involve the body.
branches.cn: 前两个义项都关乎身体。

branches.en: Discomfort can be physical or mental.
branches.cn: 不适可以是身体上的，也可以是心理上的。

intro.en: Sick forms a family of illness words.
intro.cn: sick 形成一个表示疾病的词族。

latinIntro.en: Sick is Germanic; Latin aeger, sick, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: sick 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 aeger（有病的）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 他一夜之间病得更重了。

items.example: She was the sickest child in the ward.
items.exampleCN: 她是病房里病得最重的孩子。

items.example: The sickness passed in a week.
The sickly plant needed more light.
items.exampleCN: 这株病弱的植物需要更多光照。

items.meaning: the bed of a sick person

items.example: He took two days of sick leave.

definition_en: a surface at the left or right, an aspect, or one group in a dispute
core_image: 一个立方体翻过来，露出旁边另外一面
scene: 他指着房间的一侧，请人把箱子搬过去。Please move the box to this side.
sceneCN: 这里 side 是「一边」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把箱子搬到这一边。

senses.title: A surface at the left or right
senses.definition: one of the surfaces or positions to the left or right
senses.example: Please move the box to this side.
senses.why: This is the basic spatial sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的空间义项。

senses.title: An aspect
senses.definition: one part of a situation or problem
senses.definitionCN: 情况或问题的一个方面
senses.example: We must look at every side of the problem.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须看问题的每个方面。
senses.why: A thing has sides in space and in thought.
senses.whyCN: 事物在空间中有侧面，在思考中也有方面。

senses.title: One group in a dispute
senses.definition: one of the groups taking part in an argument or game
senses.definitionCN: 争论或比赛中参与的一方
senses.example: Both sides agreed to talk.
senses.why: People line up on opposite sides like two edges.
senses.whyCN: 人分站两边，就像两条边。

intro.en: Side once meant the flank of the body.
intro.cn: side 最初指身体的侧面。

items.en: Side meant a flank or a long edge.
The related word sitha also meant side.
items.cn: 相关词 sitha 同样表示侧面。

items.en: The word spread to land, rooms, and roads.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到土地、房间和道路。

items.en: The sense of aspect appeared.
The sense of a team or party appeared.

note.en: Side is compared with similar-looking words and with words for edges.
note.cn: 把 side 与形近词以及表示边缘的词作比较。

entries.definition: a place where something is or happens

normalIntro.en: Side is always the part beside you.
normalIntro.cn: side 永远是身旁的那一面。

normal.en: Please move the box to this side.
They sat side by side.
Both sides agreed to talk.
The shop is on the other side.
He took my side in the argument.

abstract.en: Every coin has two sides.
abstract.cn: 每枚硬币都有两面。

abstract.en: A side is a door into a whole.
abstract.cn: 一个侧面是通向整体的门。

abstract.en: To choose a side is to choose a story.
abstract.cn: 选边站就是选择一个故事。

examples.en: Please move the box to this side.
We must look at every side of the problem.
examples.cn: 我们必须看问题的每个方面。

examples.en: Both sides agreed to talk.

dict_mnemonic.text: side 的核心是旁边那一面：路的两旁是 side，争论的两边也是 side。

root: 源自古英语 side（肋部、侧面），核心义「旁边的一面」。

sensesIntro.en: Side means a surface at the left or right, an aspect, or one party.
sensesIntro.cn: side 意为侧面、方面或一方。

core.en: The face beside the main face.

branches.en: A box has six sides.
A problem has many sides.
Two sides meet to talk.
Space and thought both have sides.
The physical edge becomes a team.

intro.en: Side builds words for edges, paths, and directions.
intro.cn: side 构成表示边缘、路径和方向的词。

latinIntro.en: Side is Germanic; Latin latus, side, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: side 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 latus（侧面）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The side of the house is white.

items.meaning: an extra result of a medicine
items.example: The drug has few side effects.
items.exampleCN: 这种药几乎没有副作用。

items.meaning: a smaller street off a main road
items.example: They parked on a side street.

items.meaning: showing only one point of view

items.example: The two houses stand side by side.

definition_en: the ability to see, something seen, or a famous place
core_image: 远处一座塔忽然进入视野，眼睛一下亮起来
scene: 天一黑，她的视力就明显变差。Her sight is poor at night.
sceneCN: 这里 sight 是「视力」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她晚上的视力很差。

senses.title: The ability to see
senses.definition: the power of seeing
senses.example: Her sight is poor at night.
senses.why: This is the basic ability sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的能力义项。

senses.title: Something seen
senses.definition: a thing that you see, often striking
senses.definitionCN: 看到的景物，常指引人注目的
senses.example: The mountain came into sight.
senses.why: What the eyes catch becomes a sight.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛捕捉到的东西就成了景象。

senses.title: A famous place
senses.definition: a famous or interesting place visited by tourists
senses.definitionCN: 游客参观的著名或有趣的地方
senses.example: We visited the sights of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 我们参观了这座城市的名胜。
senses.why: Places worth seeing are called sights.
senses.whyCN: 值得一看的地方被称为名胜。

intro.en: Sight is related to the verb see.
intro.cn: sight 与动词 see 同源。

items.en: Gesiht meant something seen.
Seon meant to see.
The form became sight.
The word named the power of seeing.
The plural sights named famous places.
items.cn: 复数 sights 用来指各处名胜。

note.en: Sight is compared with similar-looking words and with words for seeing.
note.cn: 把 sight 与形近词以及表示看见的词作比较。

entries.definition: a surface at the left or right
what you can see from a place

normalIntro.en: Sight is what the eye can do and what it catches.
normalIntro.cn: sight 既是眼睛的能力，也是眼睛捕捉到的东西。

normal.en: Her sight is poor at night.
The mountain came into sight.
We visited the sights of the city.
normal.cn: 我们参观了这座城市的名胜。

normal.en: Keep the child in sight.
He lost sight of the boat.

abstract.en: Sight turns distance into nearness.
abstract.cn: 视力把遥远变成眼前。

abstract.en: What we see shapes what we believe.
abstract.cn: 所见塑造所信。

abstract.en: Some things are a sight for sore eyes.
abstract.cn: 有些东西是让疲惫眼睛一亮的美景。

examples.en: Her sight is poor at night.
The mountain came into sight.
We visited the sights of the city.
examples.cn: 我们参观了这座城市的名胜。

dict_mnemonic.text: sight 与 see 同源：看见的能力是视力，看见的东西是景象，值得看的地方是名胜。

root: 源自古英语 gesiht（所见），与 seon（看见）同源，核心义「看见」。

sensesIntro.en: Sight means the power to see, something seen, or a famous place.
sensesIntro.cn: sight 意为视力、景象或名胜。

core.en: The world entering through the eyes.

branches.en: Her eyes see less at night.
branches.cn: 她的眼睛夜里看得更少。

branches.en: The mountain enters the view.
Visitors walk among the sights.
Ability and image share one word.
branches.cn: 能力与影像共用一个词。

branches.en: A notable view becomes a place to visit.
branches.cn: 出众的景致变成了可游览的地方。

intro.en: Sight builds words for seeing and traveling.
intro.cn: sight 构成表示观看与旅行的词。

latinIntro.en: Sight is Germanic; Latin visus, sight, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: sight 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 visus（视觉）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The sights are worth a day.
The boat was sighted at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 那条船在黎明时被看见。

items.example: There was a sighting of the bird.
The sightless man used a cane.
items.exampleCN: 那位失明的男人拄着拐杖。

definition_en: a mark with a meaning, a fact showing something, or a notice board
core_image: 门上一块木牌，白字写着方向
scene: 门上挂着一块牌子，上面写着「推」。The sign on the door says Push.
sceneCN: 这里 sign 是「招牌、告示牌」（第 3 个义项）；句意：门上的牌子写着「推」。

senses.title: A mark with meaning
senses.definition: a mark or symbol that carries a meaning
senses.definitionCN: 带有含义的记号或符号
senses.example: The plus sign means add.
senses.why: This is the basic symbolic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的符号义项。

senses.title: A fact showing something
senses.definition: something that shows a fact or a likely event
senses.definitionCN: 表明某个事实或可能发生之事的现象
senses.example: There is no sign of rain.
senses.why: Facts act like marks that point to more.
senses.whyCN: 事实就像指向更多信息的记号。

senses.title: A notice board
senses.definition: a board or notice that gives information or a warning
senses.definitionCN: 提供信息或警告的牌子
senses.example: The sign on the door says Push.
senses.why: A board is a large public mark.
senses.whyCN: 牌子是一种大型的公共记号。

intro.en: Sign comes from the Latin word for a mark.
intro.cn: sign 来自拉丁语中表示记号的那个词。

items.en: Signum meant a mark or token.
The word passed into French as signe.
items.cn: 这个词以 signe 的形式进入法语。

items.en: English borrowed it as signe.
The spelling became sign.
The verb use meant to write one's name.
items.cn: 动词用法表示写下自己的名字。

note.en: Sign is compared with similar-looking words and with words for marks.
note.cn: 把 sign 与形近词以及表示记号的词作比较。

entries.definition: to make music with the voice
a mark that stands for something
a sign of what will happen

normalIntro.en: A sign is a small mark that points beyond itself.
normalIntro.cn: sign 是一个指向自身之外的记号。

normal.en: The sign on the door says Push.
There is no sign of rain.
The plus sign means add.
He signed his name at the bottom.
The driver missed the stop sign.

abstract.en: A sign is a finger pointing at meaning.
abstract.cn: 记号是指向意义的一根手指。

abstract.en: Small marks carry large agreements.
abstract.cn: 小小的记号承载着重要的约定。

abstract.en: What we notice becomes a sign.
abstract.cn: 被我们注意到的东西就成了迹象。

examples.en: The sign on the door says Push.
There is no sign of rain.
He signed his name at the bottom.

dict_mnemonic.text: sign 的核心是「记号」：小记号是符号，指向事实是迹象，挂在门上就是招牌。

root: 源自拉丁语 signum（记号、标志），核心义「有含义的记号」。

sensesIntro.en: Sign means a meaningful mark, a sign of a fact, or a notice board.
sensesIntro.cn: sign 意为有含义的符号、迹象或告示牌。

core.en: A visible mark that points to something else.

branches.en: A plus sign stands for addition.
Dark clouds are a sign of rain.
A board tells people what to do.
branches.cn: 牌子告诉人们该怎么做。

branches.en: Both senses point beyond the mark.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都指向记号之外。

branches.en: Public marks turn facts into warnings.
branches.cn: 公共记号把事实变成警告。

intro.en: Sign builds a large family of marking and meaning words.
intro.cn: sign 构成一个表示标记与含义的大家族。

latinIntro.en: Sign comes through French from Latin signum, a mark.
latinIntro.cn: sign 经由法语来自拉丁语 signum（记号）。

items.example: The sign was easy to read.
The signing took place at noon.

items.meaning: a sign that gives a message

items.example: Her signature is hard to copy.
The signpost points to the lake.

definition_en: a sound, light, or action that carries a message, or a sign of something
core_image: 铁轨旁的红灯亮起，列车应声停下
scene: 火车鸣笛发出信号，缓缓启动。The train gave a signal and slowly started.
sceneCN: 这里 signal 是「信号」（第 1 个义项）；句意：火车发出信号，缓缓启动。

senses.title: A message sent by sound or light
senses.definition: a sound, light, or movement that sends a message
senses.definitionCN: 传递信息的声音、光或动作
senses.example: The train gave a signal and slowly started.
senses.exampleCN: 火车发出信号，缓缓启动。
senses.why: This is the basic message sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的信息义项。

senses.title: A traffic light
senses.definition: a set of lights that controls traffic
senses.example: Turn left at the next signal.
senses.exampleCN: 在下一个信号灯处左转。
senses.why: A light on the road is a public message.
senses.whyCN: 路上的灯是给公众的信息。

senses.title: A sign of something
senses.definition: something that shows a change or a likely event
senses.definitionCN: 表明变化或可能发生之事的现象
senses.example: The report is a signal of change.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是变化的信号。
senses.why: Any message can be read from events.
senses.whyCN: 任何信息都可以从事态中读出。

intro.en: Signal grew from the Latin word for a sign.
intro.cn: signal 由拉丁语中表示记号的词发展而来。

items.en: Signum meant a mark or sign.
Signale meant a sign or signal.
The word entered French as signal.
items.cn: 这个词以 signal 进入法语。

items.en: English used signal for messages by sound or light.
items.cn: 英语用 signal 表示声光传递的信息。

items.en: The word also named traffic lights.
items.cn: 这个词也用来指交通信号灯。

note.en: Signal is compared with similar-looking words and with message words.
note.cn: 把 signal 与形近词以及表示信息的词作比较。

entries.definition: a signal for someone to act
a sign that something is true

normalIntro.en: A signal is a message that travels through light or sound.
normalIntro.cn: signal 是借着光或声音传递的信息。

normal.en: The train gave a signal and slowly started.
normal.cn: 火车发出信号，缓缓启动。

normal.en: Turn left at the next signal.
normal.cn: 在下一个信号灯处左转。

normal.en: The phone signal was weak.
She raised her hand as a signal.
The report is a signal of change.
normal.cn: 这份报告是变化的信号。

abstract.en: A signal is a message in a hurry.
abstract.cn: 信号是匆忙上路的信息。

abstract.en: Light and sound can carry agreement.
abstract.cn: 光和声音也能承载约定。

abstract.en: Small signals prevent large accidents.
abstract.cn: 小小的信号防止大大的事故。

examples.en: The train gave a signal and slowly started.
examples.cn: 火车发出信号，缓缓启动。

examples.en: Turn left at the next signal.
examples.cn: 在下一个信号灯处左转。

examples.en: The report is a signal of change.
examples.cn: 这份报告是变化的信号。

dict_mnemonic.text: sign（记号）加 -al 变成 signal：一个记号还不够，要会发声发光的记号，就是信号。

root: 源自拉丁语 signum（记号），经中世纪拉丁语 signale 发展而来，核心义「传递信息的记号」。

sensesIntro.en: Signal means a message by sound or light, a traffic light, or a sign of change.
sensesIntro.cn: signal 意为声光信号、交通信号灯或变化的迹象。

core.en: A sign sent through the air.

branches.en: The whistle sends a signal.
The traffic signal turns red.
The report signals change.
Both are messages for many people.
branches.cn: 两者都是给许多人的信息。

branches.en: A light and a hint both guide.

intro.en: Signal builds a family of message and traffic words.
intro.cn: signal 构成表示信息与交通的词族。

latinIntro.en: Signal comes through French from Latin signum, a mark.
latinIntro.cn: signal 经由法语来自拉丁语 signum（记号）。

items.meaning: a message by sound or light

items.example: The signals were hard to see.
The signaller waved the train on.
items.exampleCN: 信号员挥手让火车前进。

items.meaning: a railway worker who works signals

items.example: The signal tower stood on the hill.

definition_en: a person's written name, the act of signing, or a distinctive feature
core_image: 笔尖在合同末尾划出熟悉的一串字
scene: 请在表格底部签上你的名字。Please put your signature at the bottom of the form.
sceneCN: 这里 signature 是「签名」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请在表格底部签名。

senses.title: A written name
senses.definition: a person's name written by that person
senses.example: Please put your signature at the bottom of the form.
senses.why: This is the basic written-name sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的书写姓名义项。

senses.title: The act of signing

senses.definitionCN: 轻松意义上的滑稽或古怪
senses.example: He made a silly face.
senses.why: Foolishness can also be playful.
senses.whyCN: 愚蠢也可以是玩闹的。

intro.en: Silly once meant happy and blessed.
intro.cn: silly 最初意为幸福的、有福的。

items.en: Saelig meant happy or blessed.
items.cn: saelig 意为幸福的、有福的。

items.en: The word meant innocent or simple.
items.cn: 这个词意为天真或单纯的。

items.en: The form became silly.
The sense shifted to foolish.
It also described playful humor.
items.cn: 它也用来形容玩闹式的幽默。

note.en: Silly is compared with similar-looking words and with words for foolishness.
note.cn: 把 silly 与形近词以及表示愚蠢的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Silly is foolishness with a smile.
normalIntro.cn: silly 是带着笑意的愚蠢。

normal.en: Don't ask such a silly question.
He made a silly face.
I made a silly mistake.
She felt silly in the big hat.
normal.cn: 戴着那顶大帽子她觉得很好笑。

normal.en: They shared a silly joke.
normal.cn: 他们分享了一个傻笑话。

abstract.en: Silly is the shadow that play casts.
abstract.cn: 傻气是玩耍投下的影子。

abstract.en: A foolish step can still make us laugh.
abstract.cn: 愚蠢的一步也能让我们发笑。

abstract.en: Children teach adults how to be silly.
abstract.cn: 孩子教大人如何犯傻。

examples.en: Don't ask such a silly question.
He made a silly face.
I made a silly mistake.

dict_mnemonic.text: silly 最初是「有福的」，后来变成「单纯的」，再变成「傻的」；记住它可以带着笑。

root: 源自古英语 sælig（有福的），词义经「天真的」演变为「愚蠢的」，核心义「缺乏判断力」。

sensesIntro.en: Silly means foolish or funny in a light way.
sensesIntro.cn: silly 意为愚蠢的或轻松可笑的。

core.en: Sense taking a holiday.

branches.en: A silly question shows weak sense.
branches.cn: 傻问题显出判断力不足。

branches.en: A funny face invites a laugh.
A small mistake is easily forgiven.
Foolish and playful often overlap.
Humor softens the foolishness.

intro.en: Silly forms a small family of foolishness words.
intro.cn: silly 构成一个表示愚蠢的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Silly is Germanic; Latin stultus, foolish, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: silly 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 stultus（愚蠢的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: That was a silly thing to say.
The game grew sillier by the minute.
A little silliness helps a party.
items.exampleCN: 一点傻气能让聚会更热闹。

items.example: A silly mistake cost him the game.
items.exampleCN: 一个愚蠢的错误让他输了比赛。

items.example: There are no silly questions in class.

definition_en: a shiny gray-white metal, objects made of it, or its color
core_image: 一枚银币在灯下翻出冷亮的光
scene: 这只戒指是银做的。The ring is made of silver.
sceneCN: 这里 silver 是「银」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这只戒指是银做的。

senses.title: The metal
senses.definition: a shiny gray-white metal used for coins and jewelry
senses.definitionCN: 用于钱币和首饰的光亮灰白色金属
senses.example: The ring is made of silver.
senses.why: This is the basic material sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的材料义项。

senses.title: Silver objects
senses.definition: knives, forks, plates, and other objects made of silver
senses.definitionCN: 用银制成的刀叉、盘子等器具
senses.example: She polished the silver before dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭前她把银器擦亮了。
senses.why: Objects take the name of their metal.
senses.whyCN: 器物以金属命名。

senses.title: The color
senses.definition: a shiny gray-white color
senses.example: He has silver hair.
senses.why: The metal names its own color.
senses.whyCN: 金属用它自己的名字命名颜色。

intro.en: Silver is an old Germanic word for the metal.
intro.cn: silver 是一个表示这种金属的古老日耳曼语词。

items.en: Seolfor meant the metal silver.
The related German word is Silber.
The form became silver.
Silverware named objects of silver.
A silver medal marked second place.

note.en: Silver is compared with similar-looking words and with metal words.
note.cn: 把 silver 与形近词以及金属词作比较。

entries.definition: a piece of money made of metal

normalIntro.en: Silver is a metal, its objects, and its color.
normalIntro.cn: silver 是金属银、银器，也是银色。

normal.en: The ring is made of silver.
She polished the silver before dinner.
normal.cn: 晚饭前她把银器擦亮了。

normal.en: He has silver hair.
She won a silver medal.
The moon sent silver light across the lake.
normal.cn: 月亮把银光洒在湖面上。

abstract.en: Silver is moonlight kept in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 银是收在抽屉里的月光。

abstract.en: Age turns hair to silver.
abstract.cn: 岁月把头发染成银色。

abstract.en: Second place still shines.
abstract.cn: 第二名也照样闪光。

examples.en: The ring is made of silver.
She polished the silver before dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭前她把银器擦亮了。

examples.en: He has silver hair.

dict_mnemonic.text: silver 一材三用：金属银、银做的器具、以及银白的光泽。

root: 源自古英语 seolfor（银），核心义「光亮灰白的金属」。

sensesIntro.en: Silver means the metal, silver objects, or the color silver.
sensesIntro.cn: silver 意为银、银器或银色。

core.en: A pale metal with a cool shine.

branches.en: The ring is pure silver.
The silver is polished for dinner.
His hair has turned silver.
The metal names the objects.
The metal gives its color.

intro.en: Silver builds a family of metal and craft words.
intro.cn: silver 构成表示金属与工艺的词族。

latinIntro.en: Silver is Germanic; Latin argentum, silver, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: silver 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 argentum（银）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The silvers were stored in a box.
A silvery light filled the room.
The silverware was set on the table.

items.meaning: a person who makes silver objects

items.example: He has been on the silver screen for years.
Her silver hair shone in the sun.
items.exampleCN: 她的银发在阳光下闪耀。

definition_en: almost the same as something else
core_image: 两片叶子并排摆着，纹路几乎一模一样
scene: 这两幅画非常相似。The two paintings are very similar.
sceneCN: 这里 similar 是「相似的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这两幅画非常相似。

senses.title: Almost the same
senses.definition: almost the same in appearance or quality
senses.definitionCN: 在外观或性质上几乎相同
senses.example: The two paintings are very similar.
senses.why: This is the basic likeness sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的相像义项。

senses.title: Of the same kind
senses.definition: of the same kind but not the same one
senses.definitionCN: 属于同一类但并非同一个
senses.example: We had similar results in both tests.
senses.exampleCN: 两次测试我们得到类似的结果。
senses.why: Things of one kind look alike.
senses.whyCN: 同类的事物看起来相像。

intro.en: Similar comes from the Latin word for like.
intro.cn: similar 来自拉丁语中表示「相像」的词。

items.en: Similis meant like or similar.
The word entered French as similaire.
items.cn: 这个词以 similaire 进入法语。

items.en: English borrowed it as similar.
The word compared qualities and shapes.
items.cn: 这个词用来比较性质与形状。

items.en: Similarity became a common noun.

note.en: Similar is compared with similar-looking words and with words for likeness.
note.cn: 把 similar 与形近词以及表示相像的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Similar means two things stand side by side in likeness.
normalIntro.cn: similar 表示两样东西在相似上并肩而立。

normal.en: The two paintings are very similar.
This word is similar to that one.
We had similar results in both tests.
normal.cn: 两次测试我们得到类似的结果。

normal.en: They solved the problem in a similar way.
normal.cn: 他们用类似的方式解决了问题。

normal.en: The twins look similar.
normal.cn: 这对双胞胎看起来很像。

abstract.en: Similar things borrow each other's shadows.
abstract.cn: 相似的事物互相借用影子。

abstract.en: Likeness helps the mind compare.
abstract.cn: 相似帮助头脑进行比较。

abstract.en: Nothing is identical, yet much is similar.
abstract.cn: 没有东西完全相同，但很多事物相似。

examples.en: The two paintings are very similar.
We had similar results in both tests.
examples.cn: 两次测试我们得到类似的结果。

examples.en: The twins look similar.
examples.cn: 这对双胞胎看起来很像。

dict_mnemonic.text: similar 来自拉丁语 similis（相像的）：不是同一个，却像一个模子刻出来。

root: 源自拉丁语 similis（相像的），核心义「几乎相同」。

sensesIntro.en: Similar means almost the same or of the same kind.
sensesIntro.cn: similar 意为相似的或同类的。

core.en: Two things sharing one shape.
core.cn: 两样东西共有一个形状。

branches.en: The paintings look almost the same.
branches.cn: 两幅画看起来几乎一样。

branches.en: Both tests gave like results.
branches.cn: 两次测试给出类似结果。

branches.en: The twins share a face.
Likeness can be in look or in kind.
branches.cn: 相似可以在外貌，也可以在种类。

branches.en: Comparison reveals the pattern.

intro.en: Similar builds a family of likeness words.
intro.cn: similar 构成表示相像的词族。

latinIntro.en: Similar comes from Latin similis, like.
latinIntro.cn: similar 来自拉丁语 similis（相像的）。

items.exampleCN: 同样地，第二次测试也失败了。

items.example: The similarity is easy to see.
Her voice is similar to mine.

definition_en: in a similar way
core_image: 两条平行的路并肩伸向远方
scene: 同样地，第二组也失败了。Similarly, the second group failed.
sceneCN: 这里 similarly 是「同样地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：同样地，第二组也失败了。

senses.title: In the same way
senses.definition: in the same or a very close way
senses.definitionCN: 以相同或非常接近的方式
senses.example: Similarly, the second group failed.
senses.exampleCN: 同样地，第二组也失败了。
senses.why: This is the basic likeness adverb.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的相似副词义项。

senses.title: Also, by comparison
senses.definition: used to add a second case that resembles the first
senses.definitionCN: 用来补充与第一种情况相似的另一例
senses.example: Similarly, prices rose in other cities.
senses.exampleCN: 类似地，其他城市的价格也上涨了。
senses.why: The adverb links two parallel cases.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词连接两个平行的例子。

intro.en: Similarly is similar plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: similarly 是 similar 加上副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Similis meant like.
The word entered French as similaire.
items.cn: 这个词以 similaire 进入法语。

items.en: English borrowed similar.
The adverb similarly joined clauses.
items.cn: 副词 similarly 用来连接从句。

items.en: It marked parallel facts in writing.
items.cn: 它在写作中标出平行的事实。

note.en: Similarly is compared with similar-looking words and with linking words.
note.cn: 把 similarly 与形近词以及连接词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Similarly puts a second case beside the first.
normalIntro.cn: similarly 把第二种情况放在第一种旁边。

normal.en: Similarly, the second group failed.
normal.cn: 同样地，第二组也失败了。

normal.en: Similarly, prices rose in other cities.
normal.cn: 类似地，其他城市的价格也上涨了。

normal.en: Both teams were similarly affected.
The two houses are similarly priced.
They think similarly about the plan.
normal.cn: 他们对这个计划的想法类似。

abstract.en: Similarly is a bridge between two facts.
abstract.cn: similarly 是两件事实之间的桥。

abstract.en: Parallel lines never meet but always agree.
abstract.cn: 平行线永不相交，却始终一致。

abstract.en: One example can quietly explain another.
abstract.cn: 一个例子能悄悄解释另一个。

examples.en: Similarly, the second group failed.
examples.cn: 同样地，第二组也失败了。

examples.en: Similarly, prices rose in other cities.
examples.cn: 类似地，其他城市的价格也上涨了。

examples.en: Both teams were similarly affected.

dict_mnemonic.text: similar（相似的）加 -ly 变副词：用相似的方式做、说或发生，就是 similarly（同样地）。

root: 由 similar（相似的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，核心义「以相似的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Similarly means in the same or a closely related way.
sensesIntro.cn: similarly 意为以相同或相近的方式。

core.en: A second fact walking in the same step.
core.cn: 第二件事实迈着同样的步子。

branches.en: The second group fails the same way.
branches.cn: 第二组以同样方式失败。

branches.en: Other cities repeat the pattern.
branches.cn: 其他城市重复这一模式。

branches.en: Two houses share a price.
The adverb links parallel cases.
branches.cn: 这个副词连接平行的情况。

branches.en: Comparison turns facts into a pattern.

intro.en: Similarly belongs to the similar family of likeness words.
intro.cn: similarly 属于 similar 这一相似词族。

latinIntro.en: Similarly comes from Latin similis, like.
latinIntro.cn: similarly 来自拉丁语 similis（相像的）。

items.meaning: to react in the same way
